problems.description: Reimplements Handlebars and EJS template engines by hand with regex-based parsing (handlebars(), ejs() functions) instead of depending on the established npm libraries; regex template parsing is fragile for nested/edge-case syntax and becomes a permanent maintenance burden.

ejs() renders expressions via Function('context', 'with (context) { ... }') — dynamic code construction with with() — which is an injection surface for untrusted templates, disallowed by common lint rules, and defeats any possibility of a static analysis safety net.
+147 lines, +7 functions, and a brand-new template/rendering subsystem shipped with zero tests despite the repo having an enforce_pytest convention.

Document wrapper collision: renderTemplate output is embedded into the existing document() full-page wrapper, yet templates may themselves emit <!doctype html> layouts (template/layout frontmatter), producing nested HTML documents that browsers and validators reject.
Extends the pre-existing operator-precedence bug in CLI option validation (&&/|| mixing) to a third option rather than fixing it — '--templates' present-but-empty still bypasses the guard.

do/while iterative re-resolution of #if/#each blocks plus repeated full-string regex passes cause runtime to scale with template size and nesting depth (cognitive complexity +9 reflects the added control flow).

Measured convention score 0.48 is driven by pre-existing violations (dev-server.ts, markdown.ts, index.ts PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_CASE rules) that this commit did not introduce; the new code itself is convention-compliant, so the headline score understates this commit's own adherence.

strengths: Feature is wired through existing extension points — BuildOptions and Page interfaces plus the buildSite flow — with no changes to call-site contracts.
New code follows repo conventions (camelCase functions, PascalCase types like TemplateContext) even though the repo-wide convention score is low.
Supports both .hbs and .ejs engines with per-file extension probing and partials loading with graceful fallback (no crash when templates dir is absent).
No new bugs, smells, or dependencies per SonarQube/AST deltas.
commit_reviews.summary: A cleanly integrated feature-addition commit that extends the existing build pipeline, but pays for it with a hand-rolled regex template engine, a Function/with() injection-prone renderer, no tests, and a nested-document layout risk — net neutral on the codebase.

problems.description: New src/server.ts module (WebSocket upgrade handling, debounced rebuild state machine, path-based file serving) ships with no test file, despite jest/ts-jest being configured.
Cognitive complexity +4 comes from the rebuilding/pending/rebuildTimer state machine in the watcher callback; correct but non-trivial control flow in a single async closure.
CLI validation bug: supplying --port without a value triggers the message 'Options --content, --output, and --templates require a directory', which misdescribes the offending option.

Convention score 0.48 with 45 violations, but the cited violations are misattributed — they reference index.ts, markdown.ts (untouched files) and 'dev-server.ts' (the new file is server.ts, and it correctly uses camelCase functions and PascalCase interfaces). Measurement appears stale or misconfigured; flagged as a discrepancy.
Adds two runtime dependencies (chokidar, ws) plus @types/ws for a dev-only server; acceptable but grows the install footprint.

strengths: Composes the existing buildSite from ./index instead of duplicating build logic — clean layering.
Path-traversal guard in serveFile returns 403 for any path escaping the output root.
close() cleanly tears down watcher, WebSocket server, and HTTP server.
Debounced rebuild with a pending flag coalesces rapid file-change bursts.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent dev-server feature that composes the existing buildSite and handles security and teardown well, but ships without tests, carries a CLI validation-message bug, and shows low measured convention adherence whose specific citations don't match this diff.

problems.description: markdownFiles() was compressed into dense single-line statements (multiple statements per line, one-line for-loop body), a readability regression vs. the original multi-line formatting
45 naming-convention violations across index.ts, dev-server.ts, markdown.ts (PascalCase classes/interfaces, camelCase functions, UPPER_CASE constants), yielding a convention score of 0.48
Dual plugin locations (plugins/*.ts barrel files re-exporting from src/plugins/*) add an indirection layer; consider consolidating so consumers import from one canonical path
resolvePlugin()'s conditional default-unwrapping logic raises cognitive complexity (+16 delta) and could be simplified or commented for clarity

strengths: Monolith split into cohesive plugin modules (markdown, template, dev-server), shrinking index.ts from 195 to 65 lines
Net line reduction (+176/-262) with zero new bugs and no duplications (0.0%)
Type-only re-exports correctly use 'export type', preserving a clean public plugin API
Backward compatible: parseMarkdown and Page remain exported from the package index
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally sound modularization that cuts the monolith down and exposes a clean plugin API, but the compacted one-line code style and 45 naming violations introduce avoidable technical debt and drag the convention score to 0.48.

problems.description: cli.ts re-parses .ssg-cache.json directly to surface build stats, duplicating cache I/O and logic that belongs inside buildSite()/index.ts; the cache file is read twice per invocation.
Silent catch that swallows cache parse errors and falls back to a hardcoded zeroed stats literal; cache corruption is indistinguishable from 'no cache' and never reported.
AST diff shows no test files added; the incremental/cache skip/invalidation paths (source hash, template hash, clean flag) are untested despite +129 lines of new logic.

Measured convention score 0.48 with 45 violations; the specific listed violations (dev-server.ts, markdown.ts PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_CASE) are in files untouched by this commit, so the low score largely reflects pre-existing state, not the new code.
Cognitive complexity +3 and smells +4 per SonarQube, concentrated in the single-line conditionals and chained logic in cli.ts/index.ts; readability suffers in the new cache/stats blocks.

strengths: Incremental build integrates cleanly with the existing BuildContext/plugin architecture via BuildCache and BuildStats exported from plugin.ts.
Cache invalidation keyed on source-content hash plus template-hash is a sound, minimal design that degrades gracefully to a full build.
Correctly disables render caching when custom onFile plugins are present (renderCacheEnabled guard), avoiding correctness bugs with plugin transforms.
New functions (templateFiles, hashFiles, readCache) are camelCase and new interfaces PascalCase, matching repo conventions in the added code.
commit_reviews.summary: A reasonable incremental-build feature that fits the plugin/context architecture and adds only +129/-10 lines, but it introduces mild technical debt through duplicated cache parsing in cli.ts, silent error swallowing, and a lack of tests for the new caching paths.

compounding_issues: Session 2 added two template/layout tests that forgot `await fs.mkdir(content, {recursive:true})`, so they failed from the moment they were written; neither session 3 nor 5 fixed them — 2/6 tests red at the final commit.

Session 4's plugin refactor broke typechecking (8→9 TS errors: MarkdownPlugin and the empty DevServerPlugin have no members in common with the Plugin interface → TS2559 cascading into TS2345/TS2339 in index.ts), so `npm run build` fails and the suite can't even compile; session 5 added a feature on top of the broken build without repairing it.

Sessions 4-5 ran in a sandbox without node/npm, so the agent shipped unverified code (session 4 reported '0 passed, 0 failed'; session 5 said execution was 'blocked locally') instead of fixing the pre-existing failures.

The refactor was partially vestigial: DevServerPlugin is an empty class and the dev server still bypasses the plugin pipeline (startDevServer calls buildSite directly), MarkdownPlugin is special-cased via `instanceof` rather than the hook system, and index.ts ↔ plugins/dev-server.ts is a runtime circular import.

Session 2's EJS engine uses `Function('context', 'with(context){...}')` — an eval-style template path with escaping inconsistency (the `-` mode returns unescaped values) carried forward into the plugin extraction unchanged.
key_decisions: Session 1: compact self-contained core (index.ts) with recursive Markdown crawl, frontmatter normalization, and escaped HTML document wrapper — a clean, testable greenfield foundation.
Session 2: hand-rolled regex-based Handlebars and EJS template engines plus per-page `template`/`layout` frontmatter selectors and shared partials — biggest feature leap, no external template deps.
Session 3: dev server with WebSocket live-reload, chokidar watching of content+templates, debounced rebuild, and path-traversal protection — solid integration layer.

Session 4: extraction into a plugin lifecycle architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), `defineConfig` + ssg.config.ts loading, and root `plugins/` re-export shims — the most consequential decision, architecturally sound in intent but implemented with type errors and leftover stubs.

Session 5: hash-based incremental build cache (.ssg-cache.json with source/template hashes, rendered-HTML reuse, stale-page cleanup, `--incremental`/`--clean`) — the cross-cutting feature, which I verified is functionally correct in isolation.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rises through the first three sessions: a clean greenfield core (2/2 tests green, tsc clean), a rich template subsystem, and a polished live-reload dev server. Session 4 marks a sharp inflection where a good architectural idea (plugin extraction) shipped unverified — the sandbox lost node/npm, so 8 type errors that break `npm run build` and make the whole test suite uncompilable went unreported. Session 5 then layers a genuinely solid incremental-build feature (its two new tests pass and cache invalidation works correctly under isolated modules) onto the broken build while ignoring the two failing template tests and the 9 type errors. Net effect: feature ambition and new-code quality stayed high, but overall project health flipped from green to red and never recovered.
story_review.summary: Architecturally coherent and genuinely cumulative across all five sessions, but the story's engineering discipline broke down in the final two sessions, leaving the repo with a failing test suite and an uncompilable build at the end.
